messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT alerted by monitoring - high error rate on Private VPC connectivity for customer ACME in us-west-2 (AZ-delta). Impact: control-plane health checks failing, application reports connection resets. Paging network oncall.
jamie: acked. I'm on-call for network today, joining. Any immediate customer-facing pages?
oncall-bot: pagerduty incident opened PD-5429. severity: sev2.
lee: joining. Which paths are failing? traceroutes from app-nodes show packet loss when hitting the transit gateway attachment.
jamie: I pulled CloudWatch for the transit attachment, seeing abrupt route withdrawals around 2026-03-14T18:12Z. BGP logs show repeated peer resets to 10.12.1.1.
alex: ping/traceroute from inside customer VPC shows next-hop dropping after AZ-delta edge. Suspect an AZ-level network fabric problem or router process crash.
sam-network: I see BGP flaps from our DirectConnect peer in us-west-2c -> us-west-2d range at 18:11:xx. AS paths get prepended then withdrawn. Filing ticket with provider NOC now.
jamie: quick ops checklist: 1) confirm scope (single AZ vs region) 2) check route table changes 3) failover to backup path if available.
lee: scope: ACME reports connectivity only from their instances in AZ-delta; inter-AZ traffic to other AZs works. So it's AZ-scoped.
jamie: running `aws ec2 describe-transit-gateway-attachments --filters Name=resource-type,Values=vpc` to list attachments in the affected zone.
infra-bot: command result: transit-attachments: tgw-attach-0a1b2c3d (us-west-2d) state: available; tgw-attach-0d3c2b1a (us-west-2c) state: available. No detach events in last 48h.
lee: checking VPC route tables for the ACME VPC - routes to 10.200.0.0/16 via tgw-attach-0a1b2c3d are present.
alex: doing `show ip bgp neighbors` on the edge router (supporting AZ-delta). Output: `Neighbor 10.12.1.1: state=Idle -> Active -> Idle` repeated, reason: socket closed by peer.
jamie: that matches provider NOC notes about instability on their edge in that AZ. Sam, any ETA from provider?
sam-network: NOC response: "We're investigating an edge software restart in AZ-delta, applying safety rollback. No ETA yet. We'll escalate to infra-engineering." I've opened ticket NOC-7781.
tessa-cust-success: pinging ACME SLA contact to inform them we're investigating and have engaged cloud provider. Drafting message: "We're investigating PrivateLink connectivity issues from your AZ-delta instances; we're routing to backup where possible and will update every 10 min"
jamie: mitigation options: A) shift traffic off AZ-delta by updating route priorities (if multi-AZ attachment available) B) advertise a blackhole/withdrawal to encourage failover on customer side C) engineer a temporary NAT/relay via another AZ.
lee: can we update transit gateway route propagation to prefer attachment in us-west-2c? If their workloads are multi-AZ, shifting to us-west-2c would restore connectivity quickly.
jamie: we can push a policy route: `aws ec2 replace-transit-gateway-route --transit-gateway-route-table-id tgw-rtb-0x --destination-cidr-block 10.200.0.0/16 --blackhole` temporarily then re-add via healthy attachment. But blackholing has risk. Prefer update to point to alternate attachment: `--transit-gateway-attachment-id tgw-attach-0d3c2b1a`.
alex: note: must coordinate with ACME to avoid asymmetric routing. If we route their VPC traffic via different AZ without their instance-level awareness, some connections may still fail. Need to confirm ACME has failover on application side.
tessa-cust-success: ACME responding: "We have multi-AZ listeners but sticky sessions might keep some traffic tied to AZ-delta instances. We'll remove stickiness shortly" - expected 10-15m.
sam-network: provider NOC just updated: "We've rolled back faulty edge software in AZ-delta and are stabilizing BGP sessions. Some flaps remain; next check in 5m."
lee: I'm seeing peer state improve; BGP neighbor 10.12.1.1 moved to Established at 18:25:04Z. Route table shows previously withdrawn prefixes reappear.
jamie: marking customer impact as partial for now. Triage note: cause = provider edge restart in AZ-delta causing BGP session resets, resulting in route withdrawal to ACME prefixes.
alex: still seeing application-level 502s for a small subset of requests due to half-open connections; likely clients stuck on AZ-delta backend. Recommend we trigger a rolling restart of the AZ-delta fleet for ACME (via their app team) or move load balancer weights.
tessa-cust-success: ACME confirms they've removed stickiness and drained AZ-delta nodes. They report reduced errors.
jamie: timeline update for internal record: detection 2026-03-14T18:12Z, provider edge restart ~18:14Z, BGP flaps until 18:25Z, customer drain completed 18:33Z, full recovery observed by 18:36Z. Impact window ~24 minutes.
lee: any follow-ups? I suggest we: 1) ask provider for RCA and change control logs, 2) add alert for rapid BGP peer flaps on AZ edges, 3) run a tabletop with the oncall runbook for AZ-scoped route instability.
sam-network: NOC replies ticket NOC-7781: "Root cause: automated edge software patch triggered a faulty process restart. Mitigation: rollback applied. RCA scheduled. We're adding guardrails to patch rollout."
jamie: I'll update incident record PD-5429 with summary and customer impact, and mark as resolved once provider confirms RCA posting.
infra-bot: incident updated: severity downgraded to investigational.
tessa-cust-success: messaging to ACME: "Issue resolved. Root cause: provider edge software restart impacting BGP sessions. We have drained affected AZ and verified connectivity. We'll share provider RCA once available. Please reopen if you see residual errors."
jamie: closing notes: total impacted customer clusters: 1 major customer (ACME) across AZ-delta only. No data loss, transient connectivity. Follow-ups: supplier RCA, new BGP-flap alert tuning, runbook amendment for option to automatically shift route priorities for multi-AZ VPCs.
alex: adding a short postmortem stub to the incidents channel referencing PD-5429 and NOC-7781.
oncall-bot: Incident PD-5429 marked resolved at 2026-03-14T18:45Z.
jamie: thanks team. Great coordination. :thumbsup:
